title: InjectionEvent
description: One event of a scenario's injected sequence. A line of scenarios/.replay/**/plan.jsonl carries `applied: null`; a line of a run bundle's injection.log.jsonl carries the same object with `applied` filled in. docs/plans/M5-implementation-plan.md section D1 and ADR-035 own the plan/apply split; docs/protocols/data-management.md section 1 names injection.log.jsonl the injected event sequence and section 3 requires it to match the scenario's ground-truth event count. Fields are `origin: engineering`: the submitted chapters define no injection-event format.

schema_version.description: A non-numeric token, so a consumer can only test it for membership in a known set rather than order it.

scenario_id.description: SCN-<CLASS>-<nn>, docs/07-glossary-and-ids.md section Scenario & injection IDs.

injection_condition.description: The grid's fifth dimension. INJ-NONE is a coordinate, not an absence: see scenarios/manifests/README.md.

seed.description: The seed this plan was drawn at. The fixed seed set lives in docs/07-glossary-and-ids.md section Seeds and is deliberately NOT enumerated here (.agents/rules/00-source-of-truth.md).

event_id.description: SHA-256 over the canonical projection of this event's identifying fields, lowercase hexadecimal. A digest, never a generated identifier -- the same construct monitor/aggregator/models.py fixes for EvidenceEvent, and for the same reason.

event_rank.description: The planner's tie-break within one offset_ms. Third key of the total order (offset_ms, event_rank, event_id); a sort on two keys leaves ties broken by insertion order (ADR-019).

offset_ms.description: Logical milliseconds from t0. The planner has no t0 to read, so no absolute time can appear in a plan -- which is what makes the determinism diff a cmp over bytes rather than a comparison that must first exclude a clock.

kind.description: `incident` events fire the scenario's incident and are present under every injection condition including INJ-NONE. `injection` events carry adversarial content at the agent layer and are absent under INJ-NONE.

injection_class.description: Null exactly when kind is `incident`. Bound in source order at M0-T0.7 finding 6; the A-D lettering is the kit's.

mechanism.description: Which harness applies this event. `chaosmesh` a fault CRD, `cve` a vulnerable-image swap, `attacker` a seeded attacker step, `workload` a benign perturbation of the target application.

primitive_id.description: References a primitive_id declared by this scenario's manifest. The manifest owns what the primitive is; the plan owns when it fires.

target.description: The object this event acts on, or null for an event with no single object. `replica_index` is drawn from the seeded generator when the workload has identical replicas (section D13).

payload_id.description: The adversarial-content instance drawn from this injection class's pool, or null on an incident event. The pool lives in scenarios/attackers/content/; the id is what makes the draw auditable without the plan carrying the payload text.

detail.description: Per-primitive parameters. Scalars only, so a plan line stays comparable byte for byte and no nested ordering can differ between two processes.

applied.description: Null in a plan. Filled by the applier in injection.log.jsonl, and it is the only place a wall clock or a run identifier enters this record -- which is what keeps scripts/scenario_determinism.sh a cmp over whole files rather than a diff that must first hold a field out (contrast ADR-019's latency.json).

run_id.description: RUN-<COND>-<SCN>-<INJ>-<SEED>, docs/07-glossary-and-ids.md. Recorded by the applier and never read by the planner: run_id carries the arm token, and a planner that keyed its generator on it would give one cell a different attack in every arm, which is exactly the confound the ablations are taken across.
